title: Audited entity merge and split: a merge is a write (retired + merged_into), reads resolve the old id and keys to the survivor, nothing under the old id is rewritten, split is the explicit reverse
context: Follow-on to state.entity-identity (dec_a33cccdcb7): one active entity per external key settles the common case, but one clinic under two CRM sites cannot be settled by a ref. dec_b4d64d643a asked for merge/split recorded as ledger events with provenance, never silent rewrites. Shipped on branch feat/entity-merge (stacked on feat/entity-identity).
decision: Add optional `merged_into` to nuryel.entity/1 (schema refinement: only on a retired entity, never itself). writeState validates the survivor (on record in the partition, within grants, active — merging into an entity that was itself merged is refused naming the one that stands now) and emits the ledger's `retired` change (the enum's first writer) for an entity leaving service. The entity index follows `merged_into` chains (cycle-safe) so a read for the old id, or any key it carried, resolves to the survivor and returns both histories as one state of record with only the survivor current; a commitment or derived statement written under the retired id or its keys is refused `identity` naming the survivor. Records filed under the retired id are never rewritten. Once retired, the entity's keys are free and the survivor may carry them. Split = re-key or retire the survivor, then write the entity active again without merged_into; refused while any active entity carries its keys.
consequences: Subscribers see `retired` for the first time; a consumer filtering on created/updated/superseded only will miss merges — the enum existed since 1.25.0.
A chain A→B→C resolves on read; a long chain costs one entity scan per read (fine at drawer scale).
Per-record re-homing of history is never done; if David wants a merged clinic's old commitments to carry the survivor's subject, that is a new decision.
alternatives_rejected: Re-key the retired entity's commitments and summaries to the survivor's subject on merge — REJECTED: ids derive from the subject, so every re-keyed record would be a new identity and the old ones a second copy; history must stay where it was written and be read through the alias.

Merge by absorbing the retired entity's refs into the survivor automatically — REJECTED: a silent rewrite of the survivor; the writer adds the refs in its own write, which the uniqueness guard now allows because the keys are free.
A dedicated `merge` verb — REJECTED: one more surface to bind on MCP/HTTP/CLI; a merge is a write of the entity with two fields, idempotent and replayable like every other write.
